title: A Low-mass Cold and Quiescent Core Population in a Massive Star Protocluster
question: Characterize the initial conditions of star and cluster formation in massive star-forming regions by searching for and studying starless and pre-stellar cores in the massive infrared dark cloud NGC 6334S.

data.angular_resolution: 3.6" x 2.4" (P.A. = 81 deg) for continuum; 4.1" x 2.8" (P.A. = 83 deg) for lines (~0.02 pc spatial resolution)
data.sensitivity: 6 mJy beam^-1 per 0.21 km s^-1 (lines); 30 uJy beam^-1 (continuum)

what.value: 49 continuum dense cores and their masses/kinematics in NGC 6334S, and clump mass of 1.3 x 10^3 M_sun

evidence.quote: With a mass of 1.3 $\times \, 10^{3} \, M_{\odot}$ (cite: 2020ApJ...896..110L)
A study of 49 continuum dense cores (hereafter continuum cores) revealed by the 3 mm wavelength continuum image was presented in (cite: 2020ApJ...896..110L)

what.value: Young stellar object (YSO) counterparts in NGC 6334S

evidence.quote: and with no young stellar object (YSO) counterparts (cite: 2013ApJ...778...96W).

what.value: Herschel/PACS 70 um data and 3-sigma sensitivity of ~0.3 Jy

evidence.quote: A 3$\sigma$ sensitivity of $\sim$0.3 Jy from `Herschel`/PACS 70 $\mu{}$m observation is used to derived an upper limit ($\sim$1.26 $L_{\odot}$) of internal luminosity for the identified NH$_{2}$D cores (cite: 2017A&A...602A..77T)

recipe.goal: Identify compact NH2D cores and extract morphological and flux parameters
recipe.method: Preselect compact structures from the NH2D velocity-integrated intensity map (-11.5 to 5.6 km s^-1) using astrodendro, filter out structures associated with continuum cores, YSOs, multiple peaks, or extreme elongation (major/minor >= 3), and fit 2D Gaussians with CASA-imfit.
key_parameters: velocity integration range = -11.5 to 5.6 km s^-1; astrodendro min_value = 3 sigma (1 sigma ~ 0.02 Jy beam^-1 km s^-1), min_delta = 1 sigma, min_npix = 40, peak >= 6 sigma

recipe.goal: Check for protostellar activity and estimate internal luminosity upper limits
recipe.method: Search for outflow signatures in HCO+, CS, HCN, SO, HNCO and H2O maser emission, inspect 3.6 to 70 um infrared images for continuum sources, and compute internal luminosity upper limits from Herschel/PACS 70 um 3-sigma flux.
assumptions: Empirical L_int - F_70 relationship from Dunham et al. (2008)

recipe.goal: Fit NH2D line kinematics and derive velocity dispersions
recipe.method: Fit the NH2D hyperfine line cube pixel-by-pixel and on core-averaged spectra, then remove channel-width smearing in quadrature to obtain intrinsic velocity dispersion and Mach number.
key_parameters: channel width sigma_ch = 0.089 km s^-1; sound speed c_s(10 K) = 0.19 km s^-1
assumptions: Temperature T = 10 K for thermal velocity dispersion and sound speed

recipe.goal: Estimate core gas masses, H2 column densities, virial masses, and virial parameters
recipe.method: Compute M_gas and N_H2 from 3 mm (98.5 GHz) continuum emission (or 3-sigma upper limits where peak <= 3 sigma) assuming optically thin modified blackbody emission, and compute M_vir and alpha_vir = M_vir/M_gas from effective radius and total velocity dispersion.
assumptions: T_dust = 10 K; gas-to-dust ratio eta = 100; dust opacity kappa_98.5GHz = 0.235 cm^2 g^-1 (beta = 1.5); mean molecular weight mu = 2.8 for N_H2 and <m> = 2.37 m_H for sigma_tot; density profile power-law index b = 2; no external pressure

recipe.goal: Derive NH2D fractional abundances and NH3 deuterium fractionation
recipe.method: Calculate N(NH2D) and abundance X(NH2D) = N(NH2D)/N(H2), fit JVLA core-averaged NH3 (1,1) and (2,2) spectra with PySpecKit to obtain T_k and N(NH3) (or 3-sigma upper limits), and compute D_NH3 = N(NH2D)/N(NH3).
assumptions: Constant temperature of 10 K and ortho-to-para ratio of 3 for NH2D; ortho-to-para ratio of 1 for NH3; T_ex = 10 K for NH3 non-detections

answer_key.quantity: Number of identified low-mass starless NH2D core candidates

evidence.quote: With the ALMA observations at a $\sim$0.02 pc spatial resolution, we identified 17 low-mass starless core candidates that do not show any evidence of protostellar activity.

answer_key.quantity: Number of gravitationally bound pre-stellar core candidates

evidence.quote: Nine out of the 17 cores are gravitationally bound, and therefore are identified as pre-stellar core candidates.

answer_key.quantity: NH2D core diameters

evidence.quote: They have diameters ranging from 0.018 to 0.04 pc (see Table 1).

answer_key.quantity: Upper limit on internal luminosity of NH2D cores

evidence.quote: The upper limit on the internal luminosity ($L_{\rm int}$) of NH$_{2}$D cores is estimated to be $\sim$1.26 $L_{\odot}$ using `Herschel`/PACS 70 $\mu{}$m data (cite: 2017A&A...602A..77T).

answer_key.quantity: Mean observed velocity dispersion across NH2D cores

evidence.quote: All the NH$_{2}$D cores show small velocity dispersion ($\langle \sigma_{\rm obs} \rangle \sim$ 0.16 km s$^{-1}$) and the majority of them are smaller than the sound speed, $c_{\rm s}$(10 K) = 0.19 km s$^{-1}$.

answer_key.quantity: Mean observed velocity dispersion of core M1

evidence.quote: For M1, pixel by pixel fit to the NH$_{2}$D line cube yields a small mean velocity dispersion $\langle \sigma_{\rm obs} \rangle \approx$ 0.107 km s$^{-1}$ (Figure 4)

answer_key.quantity: Intrinsic observed velocity dispersion of core M1

evidence.quote: corresponding to an intrinsic observed velocity dispersion of $\sigma_{\rm obs,int}$ = 0.06 km s$^{-1}$ after removing the smearing effect due to the channel width

answer_key.quantity: Upper limit on gas kinetic temperature of core M1 from thermal broadening

evidence.quote: Assuming the observed linewidths of the NH$_{2}$D line are caused only by thermal broadening, the gas temperature is found to be about 7 K, $\sigma_{\rm th,NH_{2}D}$(7 K) = $\sigma_{\rm obs,int}$ = 0.06 km s$^{-1}$.

answer_key.quantity: Gas mass range of NH2D cores

evidence.quote: The derived cores masses are between $<$ 0.13 and 0.87 $M_{\odot}$, with a mean value of 0.45 $M_{\odot}$ (Table 1).
